subject: Pricing & batching follow-up — token volumes, unit economics, continuous batching assumptions
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap — token volumes & batching follow-up

Hi Emma — thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick recap + next steps from our side.

Summary of what I heard:
- Primary workload: conversational product recommendation assistant (chat-style flows).
- Monthly token volume (estimated): ~1.2B tokens / month (prompt + completion).
- Typical session: 2-6 turns, median completion length ~60-80 tokens, heavy tail to 600+ tokens on some workflows.
- Concurrency / pattern: steady-state QPS ~12-20, peak concurrent requests ~150-220 (peaks during morning/evening).
- Primary goals: keep latency P90 under 600ms, target unit economics ~$100 / 1M tokens (open to a range).

Notes on price expectations & ask:
- You mentioned a target of $80-120 / 1M tokens and a monthly budget band - confirm if ~$100 / 1M tokens is still the right target for us to design around.
- We can model both Hosted (usage-based) and Dedicated (reserved capacity) options; dedicated typically gives better per-token economics at high sustained volume but requires a commit.

Batching & caching assumptions we should validate:
- Continuous batching: for chat-style short requests, our runtime performs continuous batching (small aggregation windows) that significantly improves throughput vs per-request execution. For workloads like yours we typically see a 20-35% reduction in effective per-token cost from batching alone (depends on QPS and request size distribution).
- KV/prefix caching: repeated prompts or system prompts can reduce prompt-token usage by 10-30% (depends on how much of the prompt can be cached).
- Concurrency sensitivity: cost/latency tradeoffs are driven by the peak concurrency and allowed batching latency - we'll tune batch window to hit your 600ms P90 SLO.

Attached: MAP_token_estimates.xlsx - I populated two scenarios (conservative / aggressive) based on the numbers above.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm the monthly token estimate and budget target ($/1M).
2) Intro call with our Solutions Engineer (Marissa) to review the MAP and run a quick batch/concurrency sketch for your traffic pattern - can do 30-45m.
3) We'll follow with a short pricing proposal (hosted vs dedicated) and sample unit-econ calc.

If that looks good I can send a calendar invite for a SE deep-dive.

Thanks - Camila

Hi Camila - this looks right, thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Monthly tokens: target ~1.2B tokens/month (this is the expected production run rate for Q4; pilot this quarter will be smaller).
- Budget: the finance sponsor is comfortable with a $90-110 / 1M tokens target; $100 / 1M is an easy baseline for conversations.
- Concurrency: peak concurrent requests tends to be ~180 (could spike to ~220 during launches). Steady-state QPS closer to 15.
- Workload detail: many sessions are short (50-120 tokens), but we have a non-trivial tail (search-augmented flows) that produce 300-800 token completions ~8-12% of the time.

Two questions for the SE call:
1) Given our short median response lengths, how effective is continuous batching vs. naive per-request execution (ballpark % improvement)?
2) For dedicated/reserved pricing, what's the break-even committed volume vs hosted?

We're happy to do the SE deep-dive next week - Tue/Wed morning PT works for us.

Great - thanks for confirming the numbers, Emma. Quick answers and a ballpark unit-econ sketch before the SE call.

1) Continuous batching effectiveness (ballpark):
- For short median responses (50-120 tokens) + steady QPS ~15 and peaks ~180, we typically observe ~20-30% effective per-token cost reduction vs per-request execution due to more efficient kernel utilization and fewer small underutilized batches. The improvement increases with higher QPS and smoother arrival distributions; for very bursty traffic it can be lower.

2) Caching impact:
- If you can cache system prompts and repeated user prefixes, expect another ~10-25% reduction in prompt token usage (depends on reuse). This is additive to batching improvements.

3) Ballpark unit economics (examples):
- Baseline hosted sticker price for this convo (example): $100 / 1M tokens.
- Baseline cost @ $100 per 1M: 1.2B tokens = 1,200 * $100 = $120,000 / month.
- Estimated with continuous batching (25% improvement) -> effective $/1M ~ $75 -> monthly ~$90,000.
- Estimated with batching + caching/quantization advances (combined ~30-35% improvement) -> effective $/1M ~ $65-70 -> monthly ~$78k-84k.

4) Dedicated vs Hosted (quick note):
- Dedicated reserved capacity frequently gives an extra step-change (lower $/1M) at the cost of a commit. For your sustained 1.2B/month profile, we can model a 6-12 month commit that targets an effective $/1M in the low-to-mid $60s (depending on CPU/GPU mix, quantization). We'll put concrete numbers in the follow-up proposal.

Next step: I'll loop in Marissa (SE) to propose two available slots Tue/Wed AM PT and we'll run the MAP+batching sketch live. I attached the MAP file with conservative/aggressive scenarios - we can iterate.

Would you like us to include a short latency forecast table (P50/P90) for each scenario on the call?

Thanks - Camila
